root_cause.text: The validation check for wire_order[i] used a greater-than comparison against ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins) instead of greater-than-or-equal, allowing an index equal to the array size and causing out-of-bounds access when the value is used to index config_pins[wire_order[i]].
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))` to `if (WARN_ON(wire_order[i] >= ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins)))`, and the commit description explicitly states that the original condition allowed wire_order[i] to equal ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins), which results in out-of-bounds access because config_pins has 4 elements (indices 0–3).

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the core vulnerable statement. This leads to out-of-bounds access when wire_order[i] is later used as an index into config_pins[wire_order[i]].

This assignment extracts the value that becomes the index into config_pins. The mask (0x0F) can produce values up to 15, which is equal to ARRAY_SIZE(config_pins) (assuming 16 pins). Since the validation check is flawed, this value can pass through and cause out-of-bounds access when used as an index.

This return statement follows the wire_order validation check. It is executed only when the WARN_ON condition is true (i.e., when wire_order[i] > ARRAY_SIZE). However, when wire_order[i] equals ARRAY_SIZE, the condition is false, so the function does not return with error, allowing the out-of-bounds index to proceed.

This adjacent validation check for analog_line uses the correct comparison operator (greater-than) for a zero-indexed array of size 8. It contrasts with the flawed wire_order check and indicates the pattern that should have been used for wire_order (i.e., >= ARRAY_SIZE). Its presence highlights the inconsistency in bounds checking.
